title: How do we write a billion and a trillion as powers of ten?
description: In the international system each name is a thousand times the one before. We find the powers of ten for a billion, a trillion and a quintillion, and compare a googol with the number of atoms in the universe. Keeko doubts how the powers combine.
teaching_notes: One idea: each new name multiplies by a thousand, so each name adds three to the power of ten. Watch for students who multiply the powers, for example six times three, instead of adding three.

source: Find the powers of 10 for a billion, a trillion and a quintillion, and compare a googol with the number of atoms in the universe
video_script.why: Each international name is a thousand times the one before, and multiplying powers of ten adds the powers, so each name raises the power by three.
video_script.substitution: Write each name as a thousand times the name before it, add three to the power, and subtract the powers to compare a googol with the atoms.
video_script.anchor: the names million, billion, trillion, quadrillion and quintillion, and a googol
video_script.wrong_answer: a billion is ten to the power eighteen
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the power of a million by the power of a thousand, six times three, and says a billion is 10 to the power 18. Multiplying by a thousand adds three zeroes, so the power goes from 6 to 9.
video_script.payoff_line: Each name multiplies by a thousand, so each name adds three to the power

final_answer.value: Billion 10 to the power 9, trillion 10 to the power 12, quintillion 10 to the power 18; a googol is far larger
final_answer.spoken: A billion is ten to the power nine. A trillion is ten to the power twelve. A quintillion is ten to the power eighteen. A googol is far larger than the number of atoms.

maths_rules: a googol = 10¹⁰⁰; atoms are at most 10⁸²; 10¹⁰⁰ ÷ 10⁸² = 10¹⁰⁰⁻⁸² = 10¹⁸, so a googol is at least 10¹⁸ times as many
the slip: 6 × 3 = 18 gives 10¹⁸, which is a quintillion
video_script.design: A row of tens is drawn for each name, and every new name adds three tens to the row before it. The working area writes the sum of the powers in a second colour.
open_questions: The atoms in the universe are 10 to the power 78 to 82 in the book; the comparison uses the larger value, so a googol is at least 10 to the power 18 times as many.

<bookmark mark='west'/>Big numbers also have names in the international system: million, billion, trillion, quadrillion and quintillion.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write a billion, a trillion and a quintillion as powers of ten.
<bookmark mark='gog'/>Then compare a googol with the number of atoms in the universe.

<bookmark mark='six'/>Three plus three is six, so a million is ten to the power six.
